videos.script: The usual picture of pair programming is a senior engineer watching a junior type, and correcting them. It is the least useful version there is. {{title}} This lesson starts with the two roles. The driver works on the line in front of them. The navigator thinks a few steps ahead. They swap often. {{roles}} In strong style, the person with the idea never types it. It goes through somebody else's hands. {{strong}} Then the honest question. Pairing costs more hours per task. When is that worth it? On hard tasks, on knowledge only one person has, and on somebody's first weeks. {{when}} Then the whole team at one keyboard, rotating every few minutes. {{mob}} And the hardest part for a senior engineer pairing with a junior: keeping your hands off the keyboard.
